answer: Each agent registers a knoll‑indexed stake of ferrous tokens that is locked for a nebula‑length epoch; the protocol groups agents by correlated stake signatures and caps the total reward per cluster. When an agent splits into N identities, the cap is divided equally, so each fake receives only 1/N of the original payout while still posting the full stake. The attacker must therefore lock 100 ferrous tokens per fake identity and forfeit the entire stake if any cluster exceeds the cap, making the cost 100 tokens × N.
